title: PINN Design Stack & Feedback Loops
description: A ten-stage design architecture showing how upstream scientific choices constrain downstream realization and how validation evidence drives targeted redesign.
represents: The stack organizes a PINN study as four coupled phases rather than as neural-network training alone. It begins with the physical problem and computational role, translates these into representation and physics-enforcement choices, realizes them numerically, and closes the loop through reliability-oriented evaluation.
interpretation: The vertical path is a typical design sequence, not a universal recipe. Bidirectional phase links indicate strong interdependence, while evaluation feedback should return the workflow to the earliest plausible design cause. A redesign is accepted only after numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, and computational-cost checks improve.

phases.title: Problem Framing
phases.summary: Defines the scientific system, numerical demands, intended PINN role, and representation interface.

phases.title: PINN Formulation
phases.summary: Defines the trainable approximation and how governing knowledge and differential operators are realized.

phases.title: PINN Training
phases.summary: Defines where objectives are enforced, how losses are balanced, and how optimization is performed.

phases.title: PINN Reliability
phases.summary: Determines whether the resulting model is numerically accurate, physically faithful, robust, efficient, and reusable.

stages.title: Physical Problem Definition
stages.subtitle: Defines the physical system and its numerical demands
stages.summary: The governing structure, geometry, conditions, scales, regularity, and available data determine every downstream design choice.

evidence.rationale: The review frames physics-informed learning around governing laws, data, and computational task, supporting problem definition as the first design layer.
The canonical PINN paper formulates forward and inverse PDE problems from equations, conditions, observations, and unknown quantities.

stages.title: Computational Role
stages.subtitle: Defines the intended use of the PINN
stages.summary: A PINN intended for forward solution, inverse recovery, discovery, control, or repeated queries requires different outputs, training data, and validation criteria.

evidence.rationale: The same PINN formulation is demonstrated for forward solution and inverse identification, making intended role an explicit design choice.
Physics-informed DeepONets change the role from one solution to a reusable parametric solution operator.

stages.title: Inputs and Outputs
stages.subtitle: Defines the representation interface
stages.summary: Input and output choices define the model interface, dimensionality, state coverage, latent variables, and quantities available for physics enforcement.

evidence.rationale: P2INNs explicitly encode PDE parameters as latent inputs, showing that the input-output interface determines reuse across a parameter family.
The foundational formulation links coordinates and observations to state fields and unknown coefficients for forward and inverse tasks.

stages.title: Representation / Architecture
stages.subtitle: Defines the trainable approximation model
stages.summary: The ansatz and basis determine approximation capacity, inductive bias, spectral behavior, derivative regularity, and optimization geometry.

evidence.rationale: Fourier-feature representation changes the learned eigenspectrum and improves multi-scale PDE approximation, directly linking basis choice to solution structure.
SAS-PINN uses a SIREN representation for high-frequency electromagnetic fields and couples it to adaptive collocation.
Locally adaptive activations with slope recovery alter the effective approximation basis and training dynamics.

stages.title: Physics Enforcement
stages.subtitle: Defines how governing knowledge constrains the model
stages.summary: Physics may enter through strong, weak, integral, hard, conservative, interface, or constitutive mechanisms with different admissibility and cost consequences.

evidence.rationale: The neural trial-solution construction satisfies boundary conditions by design, providing the historical basis for exact ansatz enforcement.
The paper compares boundary enforcement in PINNs and VPINNs and supports exact Dirichlet satisfaction as a distinct enforcement choice.
Conservative PINNs impose discrete conservation and interface flux continuity rather than relying on a pointwise PDE penalty alone.
VPINN accuracy depends on test functions and quadrature, showing that weak enforcement is a numerical formulation rather than a generic loss term.

stages.title: Differentiation and Residual Evaluation
stages.subtitle: Defines how operators and derivatives are computed
stages.summary: Derivative order and operator realization control residual fidelity, gradient quality, memory, solver calls, and numerical stability.

evidence.rationale: CAN-PINN couples automatic and numerical differentiation to change residual accuracy, support coupling, and training cost.
Hutchinson trace estimation targets the memory and runtime burden of high-dimensional, high-order automatic differentiation.
Variational residual evaluation exposes quadrature precision and test-function degree as explicit numerical choices.

stages.title: Sampling / Collocation
stages.subtitle: Defines where the loss is enforced
stages.summary: Collocation determines domain and constraint coverage and therefore which residual information enters the gradient.

evidence.rationale: A large comparative study shows that residual-point distribution materially changes PINN accuracy and sampling efficiency.
Loss-proportional importance sampling improves convergence by changing which collocation information enters each update.

stages.title: Loss Construction and Balancing
stages.subtitle: Defines the optimization objective
stages.summary: The composite objective couples data and physics; its scaling and competition determine signal quality, constraint balance, and convergence.

evidence.rationale: The paper models competitive data, boundary, initial, and PDE losses and updates their weights adaptively.
Gradient-flow analysis identifies stiffness-driven imbalance among composite PINN objectives and motivates gradient-statistic balancing.
Dual-cone descent treats boundary and PDE losses as a multi-objective gradient-conflict problem.

stages.title: Optimization and Training Strategy
stages.subtitle: Defines how the objective is minimized
stages.summary: Optimizer sequence, learning rate, initialization, curricula, transfer, and stopping determine convergence speed and stability.

evidence.rationale: Loss-landscape analysis connects differential-operator ill-conditioning to optimizer behavior and compares Adam, L-BFGS, hybrid, and second-order strategies.
The study examines how optimization process and optimizer choice control achievable PINN accuracy.
A staged self-adaptive, genetic-initialization, and L-BFGS workflow demonstrates the effect of hybrid training strategy.

stages.title: Evaluation and Validation
stages.subtitle: Determines reliability and guides redesign
stages.summary: Validation must combine solution error, residual diagnostics, physical fidelity, robustness, uncertainty, inverse recovery, computational cost, and benchmarks.

evidence.rationale: The review evaluates physics-informed learning across accuracy, physical consistency, data use, and computational roles rather than by training loss alone.
B-PINNs show that noisy inverse problems require uncertainty-aware validation in addition to point prediction.
The paper separates parametric and approximation uncertainty and uses uncertainty-guided sensor placement, supporting calibrated reliability checks.

relationships.label: Problem definition constrains the intended role
Ansatz and physics must be compatible
Residual evaluation determines sampling cost and information
Point coverage determines the enforced objective
Training produces the candidate model to validate
Results may require redefining the problem

evidence.rationale: The reviewed evidence emphasizes matching physics-informed method and evaluation to the governing problem rather than assuming one universal formulation.

relationships.label: Results may require redefining the PINN role

evidence.rationale: Repeated-query evaluation motivates moving from a single PINN solve to a learned solution operator.

relationships.label: Poor performance may require changing outputs

evidence.rationale: Explicit latent parameter encoding demonstrates how revising the input-output interface changes parameterized-PDE performance.

relationships.label: Poor performance may require changing architecture

evidence.rationale: Spectral failure of standard representations motivates Fourier-feature redesign for multi-scale PDEs.

relationships.label: Reformulate physics if constraints are not satisfied

evidence.rationale: Conservation and interface-flux errors motivate a conservative discrete-domain reformulation.
Persistent boundary error motivates exact Dirichlet enforcement rather than penalty-only treatment.

relationships.label: Reformulate differentiation if residual cost is high

evidence.rationale: High-order derivative memory and runtime motivate trace-estimation reformulation.
Sparse or costly residual evaluation motivates coupled automatic–numerical differentiation.
Residual-based adaptive refinement explicitly reallocates points from current residual information.
Competitive loss progress is used to update adaptive objective weights during training.
Gradient statistics expose imbalance and drive learning-rate annealing across composite terms.

relationships.label: Adjust optimizer, learning rate, initialization, or strategy

evidence.rationale: Ill-conditioned loss landscapes motivate hybrid and curvature-aware optimizer changes.
